newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy up, but tough times may lie ahead.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy up, but tough times may lie ahead.

text.p: Best Buy Co Inc shares may have climbed after an analyst reiterated a buy rating, but the retailer and its competitors may still face a rocky period, other analysts said Thursday.
Best Buy shares closed up 1-5/8 Thursday at 12-1/2 after Salomon Brothers Inc analyst David Childe reiterated a buy rating on stronger-than-expected same store sales in February.
But Christopher Vroom, an analyst at Alex. Brown, said the consumer electronics industry as a whole could be facing a rough patch.
"We believe fiscal 1998 (calendar 1997) will continue to be a difficult one for consumer electronics retailers in general," Vroom said, citing Best Buy and Circuit City Stores Inc.

"The outlook for durable goods sales compared to non-durable goods is about to change," Vroom said. "Consumer electronics retailers will not have the underlying support they enjoyed from durable goods sales in the last few years."
"(Those retailers) had the wind at their backs, and Best Buy couldn't make its model work," Vroom said. "With the wind in a new direction, the challenge will be even greater."

The report from Salomon analyst Childe also cited a reduction in aggressive zero-percent-financing promotions, better management of Best Buy's personal computer category and a recent open market stock purchase by Chairman Richard Schulze as factors behind the buy rating reiteration.
Other analysts, however, were unsure whether Best Buy would be able to sustain the new-found momentum.

"They're still in for a tough first two quarters," John Hughes, an analyst at Piper Jaffray Inc, said. "They could get a lift from DVD (Digital Versatile Disc products), but that probably won't be until the fourth quarter."
Earlier Thursday, Best Buy announced it will begin selling DVD hardware and software on a limited basis next week and will roll out the new technology in all of its stores May 1.
Best Buy, which is expected to report fiscal 1997 earnings April 9, also recently announced it will begin reporting sales on a quarterly basis instead of monthly.
Dean Ramos, an analyst at Dain Bosworth Inc, believes Best Buy is continuing a makeover that began a few years ago.
"I see 1998 as a changeover year for Best Buy," Ramos said. "The company had lower sales near the end of the year."
"That puts a strain on the balance sheet and Best Buy will most likely have to slow down growth," Ramos said.
David Toung, an analyst at Argus Research, believes there will be a pickup in demand for products being sold at Best Buy at some point.
However, he cautions, "there is still a lot of competition, and discounting, like zero-percent financing for computers, is not going away."
